R1.title: Kitchen: a one-off change for the next time (D8)
R1.what: New first question when the customer needs a different time, the equipment's next times, the safety question, a check step, a booked card, a cancel path and a site banner. The live answer "It's fine, but we need it at different times" goes to this step instead of straight to the timetable form. "Different times every week" still goes to the live form.

R2.title: Something else, redesigned (D5, D11)
R2.what: The customer picks what it is about and the dashboard starts that issue's questions; the two agent-judgement buttons and the "it is controlled, go back" dead end are gone. "None of these" asks the universal risk question (R14) in place of the live urgent-or-not question, and the live required reason box becomes the shared mandatory P1 comment.

R3.title: Hot water: one closed note everywhere (D5, D7)
R3.what: No hot water control and no temperature reading at any site, so the two agent buttons ("Pass it to the IoT team", "Scope guidance") are removed and the screen goes straight to a closed note telling the customer to use their service contractor. The hot water state at the time of the call is added to the ticket.

R4.title: Not on Lighthouse here: closed note, no dead end (D6, D11)
R4.what: Outside lighting, extractor fans, heating and air conditioning that are not on Lighthouse at the site now end on a closed note (with "Which equipment is it?" as in live kitchen), instead of "Continue under Something else". Live air conditioning is the same at every site; it now says so honestly where there is none.

R5.title: Connection check: no button, divert corrected (D10)
R5.what: The "Run connection check" button on the site screen and the typed keywords are removed (the automatic divert stays). The divert no longer says "Everything at this site is online" when the customer's own thermostat is the thing that is offline. The all-online screen is no longer reachable.

R6.title: Heating (thermostats): customer questions, no agent buttons (D5, D12)
R6.what: The agent buttons "Give the radiator advice", "Raise the setpoint anyway" and "Adjust the setpoint anyway" are replaced by plain questions to the customer (for example "Are the radiators in that area warm?"); the turn-it-off card asks the customer. The area picker and readings are live.

R7.title: Device control window: plain wording and an honest ticket line (D2, D4)
R7.what: Window titles and buttons in plain words ("Make it warmer", "Send"), no raw device codes, and "I've logged it" only when a ticket number came back (a failed ticket shows "Try logging again"). Results use the live after-card. The repeated "not confirmed yet" pop-up shows once (not visible on a screen).

R8.title: Customer details: name, role and number (D9, non-blocking)
R8.what: Asked on the site screen after the site is confirmed. The call record still starts at site confirm (live E1), so the issue buttons are never blocked. "The customer won't give these" records that instead. Once saved, a customer line appears above every issue screen.

R9.title: Tonight: plain outcome chips and "What happened"
R9.what: Raw codes replaced by plain chips (including the boiler-boost key, closed note and the kitchen one-off chips).

R10.title: "Caller" becomes "customer" in ticket text (B4)
R10.what: The words "caller" and "Caller" in ticket subjects, ticket notes and the ticket status label (views.js:99, zendesk.js:255, 388-389, 588). Shown on the "Ticket wording" screen and on the callback ticket drawer.

R11.title: Boiler-panel (pub heating) screens added to the prototype (C6a)
R11.what: These screens are live and unchanged apart from the shared text key; they were missing from the earlier prototype. The two duration results ("Heating turned on/off") are captured from live; the transient "Sending…" screens are not shown.

R12.title: Outside lighting wording: "on-site switch" becomes "manual override"
R12.what: Live uses "the on-site switch" in the lighting known-lines and the ticket text but "manual override" everywhere else (C1). Made consistent.

R13.title: Site screen "Sending nothing": offline banner hint
R13.what: The offline banner no longer offers the connection check button; its hint now reads "The questions check the equipment for you if your issue involves it."

G1.title: Grammar fixes on multi-circuit kitchen sites (D)
G1.what: "can't show whether them are on" becomes "can't show whether they are on", and "has the kitchen — pot wash and kitchen — fryers come on?" becomes "have the kitchen — pot wash and kitchen — fryers come on?".

N1.title: Example data
N1.what: Site name, house number, ticket numbers and the times shown are fixed examples so every screen reads the same; the live screens use the site's own data.

R14.title: D13: the universal risk question, the only way to a P1
R14.what: Every flow asks "Is there an immediate risk to trade or to anyone's health and safety?" (Yes / No) where the problem is still not resolved on the call, before the ticket is made. Yes goes to the live P1 confirm step and cannot be raised until the agent has written why it is urgent. No is the normal ticket for the next working day (or the closed note where Lighthouse does not control the equipment). It replaces the kitchen "is it needed for service" question, the fridge "is stock at risk" question and the Something else "is it urgent" question, and it is now the only way to a P1 (lighting, contractor, hot water, fans, heating, air conditioning, connection, not-on-Lighthouse and site-not-identified paths all go through it).

R15.title: D14: the urgency window (fans, air conditioning, kitchen times and one-offs)
R15.what: Planned requests are filtered by whether they are urgent, judged against the IoT team's office hours and a 3 working hour response. Extractor fans: one-off or every week, then when it is needed; only a one-off that is urgent can be a P1. Kitchen "different times every week": only an urgent request can be a P1. Kitchen one-off: the "will someone be there" question is gone; an urgent one-off the dashboard can make is booked, and one it cannot make raises a P1 automatically. Air conditioning keeps the risk question and tells the agent where to put an ongoing schedule change.
